We don't run a private location database, but here's a fast, privacy-friendly way to search on your own terms — either by typing your city/ZIP code, or by sharing your location with your browser only if you choose to.

Search by City or ZIP Code

We'll only access your location if you click the button above and approve your browser's permission prompt. Nothing is stored on our end — the search happens entirely in your browser.

Tips for a Better Search

  • Search "salon studios near [your city]" alongside the specific service you want.
  • Check individual stylists' social media for portfolio photos before booking.
  • Call or message ahead to confirm current pricing and availability.
  • Read our salon studio guide so you know what questions to ask.

What to Check Once You've Found a Few Options

A map search will show you locations, but it won't tell you much about the individual professionals working there. Once you've narrowed down a building or two, the next step is researching who actually works in that location — most independent stylists maintain their own Instagram or booking page separate from the location's general listing. Look specifically for recent work in the style or technique you want, rather than judging based on the location's overall star rating, which blends reviews for many different professionals.

Booking Your First Appointment

Most independent professionals in the salon-studio model handle their own booking, often through a texting service, an online booking page, or a direct phone call rather than a shared front desk. When you reach out for the first time, it helps to be specific: mention the service you want, roughly how long your hair is, and any reference photos you have. This lets the professional give you an accurate time estimate and price range before you even arrive, rather than discovering a mismatch once you're in the chair.

What If There Isn't One Nearby?

Salon-suite locations aren't in every city, and even where they exist, availability for a specific service or specialty can be limited. If a search doesn't turn up a good match, broadening your radius slightly, checking neighboring towns, or searching for the service itself ("balayage near me") rather than the business model by name often surfaces more options. A great independent stylist working outside the salon-studio model can be just as good a fit as one working inside it — the model itself is a business structure, not a guarantee of quality.
